$comment: Sites whose PAINT VALUE is runtime data. A skin rule cannot hold them, and emitting one custom
property per caller value, swatch or datum would be strictly worse code than the inline value. They are NOT
pending work: carrying them as debt that can never reach 0 is a lie in the ratchet, and it sends
migration agents chasing an impossible zero.
Each entry declares one or both CHANNEL FLOORS: `floor` for inline object-literal/imperative
paint, `runtimeSvgFloor` for D3/DOM/JSX SVG, and `embeddedCssFloor` for declarations inside
real injected CSS strings/templates. The gate enforces each channel independently -- no channel
can satisfy another channel's floor -- and the floors are
what a migration's exit criterion is measured against instead of 0.
Counts come from the WO-SKIN-06 inventories (ck-e, ck-h, ck-f). Update them ONLY with a measured
recount, never to make a gate go green.

SKIN-EXEMPT-RUNTIME-VALUE.$why: The paint value is supplied at runtime: a tenant's chosen brand hex, caller-owned visual prop, per-datum chart colour, per-user identity colour, or a fidelity-preserving copy of live document paint. Static skin CSS cannot author those values.

primitives/layout/Box/engines/modern/ind.why: Box forwards the caller's free-form background/backgroundColor, border width/color/style, transform and color props. The two authored radius/shadow defaults migrate; these eight caller values must retain inline precedence.

primitives/layout/Box/engines/rustic/ind.why: Rustic Box has the same eight caller-owned paint channels as modern. They are the public primitive contract, not tenant chrome a static skin can choose.

primitives/layout/Collapse/runtime/token.why: useCollapseTokens merges the caller-owned style escape hatch after generated CSS custom properties. The opaque consumer paint bag must retain inline precedence; the runtime does not author a fixed visual value that a skin could replace.

primitives/display/Card/engines/rustic/i.why: The caller-supplied backgroundColor shorthand is intentionally forwarded into Card's style object; external CSS would change caller precedence.

primitives/runtime/overlay/backdrop/inde.why: Overlay backgroundColor is the caller-provided backdrop colour. The value is arbitrary at runtime and must continue to win inline.

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ex.why: The exporter copies runtime-computed paint into two CSSStyleDeclaration paths and five SVG presentation-attribute paths, including variable-backed attributes already present on the clone. It preserves rendered chart fidelity for export; a static skin cannot know the property/value pairs.

patterns/customization/tenant-preview/en.why: buildPaletteSteps() mixes a 10-step palette from the tenant's chosen hex (mixColor(base, '#fff'|'#000', ratio)), then renders it as swatches, buttons and badges.

The same 10 palette steps, plus 4 render sites. NOTE: rustic's Button/Input/Badge sections use generic DS scale tokens instead of the tenant's actual colour -- a real cross-engine inconsistency, filed separately, not something the migration may 'fix'.

patterns/customization/brand-studio/inde.why: index.tsx:387 -- background: isHex(value) ? value : 'transparent', the live swatch of the field the admin is typing into.

patterns/communication/presence/index.ts.why: Per-user identity colours (ringColor/cursorColor) that stay runtime-authored: the avatar ring border, avatar-initials colour, and LiveCursor name-badge background are 3 inline-counter sites; the LiveCursor SVG `fill={cursorColor}` is 1 intrinsic-SVG JSX site protected separately by runtimeSvgFloor. Together these are the 4 true-runtime sites recorded by CK-F, without letting either measurement channel substitute for the other.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/b.why: Two legend swatches and six D3 bar/gradient paint sinks consume caller- or datum-derived series colours. Both channels retain exact independent floors.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/l.why: Legend/tooltip value objects retain two runtime colour sites; five D3 line, area-gradient and dot sinks paint the same caller-derived series colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/a.why: Legend/tooltip value objects retain two runtime colour sites; eight D3 area, gradient, line and dot sinks consume caller-derived series colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/r.why: Two inline series-colour value sites (the default series colour and legend swatch) consume runtime palette or caller-supplied series colours. The four D3 polygon, emphasis and point sinks moved to the chart-engine radar renderer (2026-07-17 recount); its floor lives on that file.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/s.why: The legend swatch and two D3 point paint sinks consume per-datum or caller-palette colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/p.why: The legend swatch and D3 slice fill consume per-datum or caller-palette colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/t.why: The legend swatch and D3 tile fill consume the caller-supplied palette.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/f.why: The legend swatch consumes per-datum or caller-palette colours. The former two D3 segment sinks were consolidated into ONE segment fill in the chart-engine funnel renderer (2026-07-17 recount); its floor lives on that file.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/w.why: Four legend value/swatch sites and two D3 bar paint sinks consume the caller-overridable increase, decrease and total colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/h.why: Two legend swatches and five D3 bar, cumulative-line and point sinks consume caller-overridable colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/g.why: The legend swatch consumes caller-supplied segment colour. The four segment/needle sinks moved to the chart-engine gauge renderer (2026-07-17 recount); its floor lives on that file.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/b.why: Twelve value-object and legend sites plus eight D3 range/value/target sinks across the horizontal and vertical render paths trace to caller-overridable range, value and target colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/s.why: Three node/link value-object and legend sites plus two D3 node/link sinks consume caller- or graph-derived colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/n.why: The legend swatch and D3 node fill consume caller palette, group or per-node colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/c.why: The D3 day-cell fill is a runtime scale output derived from chart data and the caller-visible colour range.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/g.why: The D3 task-duration and task-progress fills consume each task's caller-derived colour.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/h.why: The D3 cell fill is a runtime scale output derived from chart data and the caller-visible colour range.

patterns/visualization/charts/families/s.why: Four intrinsic-SVG paint attributes consume caller-overridable line, area and point colours.

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.why: The segment fill (`fill={segment.color}`) paints the per-datum or caller-palette colour the funnel family forwards into the React renderer. Measured 2026-07-17 after the chart-engine refactor moved D3 paint out of families/funnel-chart; the former second D3 sink was consolidated into this single fill.
patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.$note: This file also carries a SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT entry; its total runtimeSvgFloor is the SUM (1 runtime-value + 1 not-paint = 2).

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.why: Four intrinsic-SVG JSX paint attributes consume runtime values: the custom segment fill (`fill={segment.color}` when colorSource is 'custom') and the caller-overridable needle paint (needle-mark fill+stroke, needle-cap fill). Measured 2026-07-17 after the chart-engine refactor moved the four D3 sinks out of families/gauge.
patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.$note: This file also carries a SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT entry; its total runtimeSvgFloor is the SUM (4 runtime-value + 4 not-paint = 8).

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.why: Four intrinsic-SVG JSX paint attributes consume the caller-supplied series colour: polygon fill+stroke, emphasis-line stroke, and point fill. Measured 2026-07-17 after the chart-engine refactor moved the four D3 sinks out of families/radar-chart.
patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.$note: This file also carries a SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT entry; its total runtimeSvgFloor is the SUM (4 runtime-value + 1 not-paint = 5).

patterns/visualization/charts/presentati.why: `TooltipValue`'s and `TooltipSeries`'s swatch `backgroundColor: color`/`backgroundColor: item.color` -- both a caller-supplied per-series/per-value color passed into the shared tooltip components every chart in the family mounts. The other 9 sites in this file (TOOLTIP_STYLE ×5, SWATCH_STYLE ×1, label colors ×3) are all static tokens.

The crosshair dot's `.attr('fill', (d) => d.color)` paints the per-datum colour supplied to the D3 overlay. CK-E's direct inventory identifies this exact B-runtime setter; runtimeSvgFloor protects it in the AST channel.

patterns/visualization/kanban-board/engi.why: Column header `borderTop: column.color ? \`3px solid ${column.color}\` : undefined` -- per-column caller-supplied accent color, no enum.
Same shape as modern: column header `borderTop`, keyed on the caller-supplied `column.color`.

patterns/visualization/calendar-view/eng.why: Event chip `background: ev.color ?? 'var(--ds-color-primary)'` -- per-event caller-supplied color.
Same shape as modern: event chip `background`, keyed on the caller-supplied `ev.color`.

patterns/visualization/map-view/engines/.why: Marker color dot `background: marker.color`, conditionally rendered only when `marker.color` is present -- per-marker caller-supplied color with NO fallback token at all (pre-existing gap, not migration-caused; every other per-item color in this checkpoint has a `?? var(--ds-*)` default, this one does not).
Same shape as modern: marker color dot `background: marker.color`, same no-fallback gap.

patterns/forms/form-builder/engines/mode.why: form-builder/engines/modern/index.tsx:282 -- the color field's read-only swatch paints `background: String(val)`, the hex the USER PICKED in that field. A value computed from data; no token set can hold it. No rustic twin (rustic renders no swatch).

surfaces/presentation/pages/experience/o.why: Nine intrinsic-SVG JSX paint attributes encode the canonical Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft provider marks. These colours are external brand identity, not tenant chrome; tokenizing them would make a skin incorrectly recolour the providers. The AST census measures exactly 9 authored paint sites in this file.

SKIN-EXEMPT-RUNTIME-VALUE.$excluded: use-chart-theme's four background-shaped domain fields belong to SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT below. Static chart paint is intentionally absent from this family and must migrate to scoped skins.

SKIN-EXEMPT-EMBEDDED-CSS-CONTRACT.$why: Source-authored CSS that intentionally remains inside a component because moving it to the global skin would change selector reach or activate behavior for unrelated consumers.

patterns/data/table-checkbox-styles/inde.why: TableCheckboxStyles is itself an opt-in CSS injector. Its seven paint declarations belong to that explicit mounted contract; globalizing them would broaden selector reach and can activate animations or hover behavior where the component was never mounted. The embedded-CSS AST/PostCSS census measures exactly 7 paint declarations.

SKIN-EXEMPT-CRASH-SAFE-FALLBACK.$why: Paint that must render when the theming provider itself has crashed. It cannot depend on a token, a skin, or anything the failure might have taken down.

surfaces/runtime/error-boundary/index.ts.why: Hardcoded hex values, deliberately. The component's own comment says it must render even when the theme provider crashes -- a token would resolve to nothing in exactly the situation this component exists for.

SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT.$why: Paint-shaped property names on objects that never reach a DOM style prop. Not A, not B: migrating them is a category error -- no CSS selector can hold a TypeScript mutation. The same law covers SVG attribute-name collisions: SMIL `fill="freeze"` on `<animate>` is animation timing state, not a colour, yet the AST fill-attribute rule counts it.

patterns/customization/brand-studio/inde.why: BrandTheme DRAFT mutations (ctl.buttonPrimary = { ..., color: v }) and a hostile-theme test fixture. The admin's keystroke is written into a theme object, not painted. Lines 229, 323, 328, 763, 765, 767, 769, 775.
patterns/customization/brand-studio/inde.$note: This file appears in two exemption families; its total floor is the SUM (1 runtime-value + 8 not-paint = 9).

surfaces/presentation/pages/operations/k.why: `color: col.color` builds the KanbanColumnDef passed to PatternKanbanBoard; it is domain-data forwarding, not a DOM style object. No CSS selector can replace this TypeScript value without changing the public column contract.

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/th.why: The four `background` keys build ChartTheme surface data returned by the hook. They never enter a React style object or DOM sink; treating them as CSS paint would be a category error.

patterns/visualization/charts/runtime/ch.why: `color: segment.color` copies the caller's per-segment colour into the immutable gauge geometry output consumed by the React renderer. It is datum forwarding inside a data structure, never a DOM style object.

One `color: segment.color` key builds the interaction datum bag forwarded to tooltips/handlers (data, not a style object), and one SMIL `fill="freeze"` on the mount `<animate>` is animation fill mode the fill-attribute rule counts as paint. Measured 2026-07-17.

One `color: segment.color` key builds the interaction datum bag (data, not a style object), and four SMIL `fill="freeze"` attributes on the track/segment/needle/value mount `<animate>` elements are animation fill mode the fill-attribute rule counts as paint. Measured 2026-07-17.

One `color: currentSeries.color` key builds the interaction datum bag (data, not a style object), and one SMIL `fill="freeze"` on the mount `<animate>` is animation fill mode the fill-attribute rule counts as paint. Measured 2026-07-17.
